description: We are a team of 6 Computer Engineering students participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project, Space Mission Design Game, focuses on interactive mission planning, resource management, engineering simulations, and AI-powered recommendations to create an engaging and educational space exploration experience.
summary:
The AESTRO AI is an interactive 3D web-based Aerospace Systems Engineering Simulation Game developed for up to 4 players. It was developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Challenge 13: Space Mission Design Game) and provides immersive experience in NASA's full-cycle end-to-end mission through the Four Mission Segments (Launch, Space, Ground, and User Segments) and Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1-4).

In direct response to the challenge, the AESTRO AI forces its players to deal with the core Systems Engineering problem – finding a balance between the 6 interrelated mission resources (Mass, Power, Budget, Data, Telecommunications, and Schedule) versus the laws of orbital mechanics (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, Keplerian mechanics, and NASA GMAT delta-Vs baselines). The player needs to assemble modular multi-stage rockets inside the realistic 3D Virtual Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB), collaborate during Flight Readiness Review process using the multi-functional Go/No-Go console, perform real-time atmospheric launch sequences and planetary Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL) missions, and study various mission anomalies benchmarked by the real NASA missions (NOAA-20, Surveyor 1, Mars 2020).

Why is AESTRO AI relevant? It brings together the complex aerospace systems engineering knowledge and gamification that can be used by students, educators, and future scientists.
details:
AESTRO AI: Orbital Command — Planetary Mission Design & Exploration Simulation

1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

AESTRO AI is an interactive, browser-based space mission engineering simulator and educational platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under Challenge 13: Space Mission Design Game. It translates authentic aerospace engineering and orbital astrodynamics into an engaging, gamified mission architecture spanning Earth Orbit (LEO), the Moon, and Mars.

The platform operates through four tightly coupled simulation engines:

  • 3D Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB) Point-Design: Players construct multi-stage launch vehicles across 6 modular subsystems: Nosecone Fairing, Avionics & Guidance, EDL Thermal Shielding, Upper Vacuum Stage, LOX/Fuel Tanks, and Main Gimbal Boosters.
  • Physics & Astrodynamics Engine: Governed by genuine aerospace principles, including the Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation (Δv = Isp · g₀ · ln(m₀/m_f)), dynamic Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR) thresholds, atmospheric aerodynamic drag curves, and staged planetary delta-V requirements (9,400 m/s for LEO, 12,200 m/s for Lunar Insertion, 15,800 m/s for Mars Jezero Touchdown).
  • Multiplayer Collaborative Flight Readiness Console: Features an authentic real-time 1–4 Player Mission Control Room where team members assume specialized flight roles (Flight Director, Propulsion Officer, Guidance & Trajectory, and Range Safety) to conduct integrated Go/No-Go countdown polling.
  • Live Telemetry & Planetary Surface Touchdown: Executes powered atmospheric ascent, stage separation, orbital insertion, and Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL) sequences with autonomous rover rollout on both Lunar craters and the Martian surface.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Democratizes Aerospace Engineering: Eliminates the steep barrier of orbital mechanics by translating mathematical formulas into tactile, real-time 3D visual feedback.
  • Immediate Scientific Feedback: Players instantly observe how payload mass, structural dry weight, specific impulse, and atmospheric densities impact mission feasibility via live radar scorecards and flight debriefs.
  • Fosters Collaborative Problem Solving: Recreates the operational pressure of NASA mission control, cultivating critical thinking, team communication, and strategic risk assessment under countdown constraints.

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

Aligned directly with NASA’s Artemis Accords and Moon-to-Mars Architecture, AESTRO AI is engineered to inspire and prepare the next generation of aerospace innovators, scientists, and software engineers.

  • Classroom STEM Integration: Serves as an open-access, zero-cost curriculum module for high schools, universities, and science museums worldwide.
  • Public Engagement with NASA Open Data: Bridges everyday citizens with genuine planetary data, transforming complex mission archives into interactive, experiential learning.
  • Scalable Research Foundation: Establishes an extensible framework ready to incorporate future exploration profiles such as Europa Clipper, Titan Dragonfly, and Near-Earth Asteroid Redirection.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, & Software Used

  • Frontend & 3D Visualization: React 18, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber (R3F), Drei, Tailwind CSS, and Lucide Icons for smooth, 60+ FPS sci-fi mission HUD interfaces.
  • Physics Engine: Custom modular TypeScript Astrodynamics Engine implementing barometric atmospheric models (Earth dense 101.3 kPa, Mars thin 0.6 kPa, Moon hard vacuum).
  • Backend & Networking: Node.js, Express, and WebSocket (Socket.io) for synchronized multi-operator telemetry and cooperative Go/No-Go polling.
  • NASA Open Data & API Assets: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), JPL Horizons Ephemeris Data, NASA Exoplanet Archive, and NOAA GOES/NESDIS Earth observation telemetry.
  • Build & Production Stack: Vite, ESBuild, Git/GitHub, Vercel Edge Cloud Deployment, and FFmpeg for high-resolution video production.

5. How Is Your Project Creative & Innovative?

  • Dual-Perspective Systems Architecture: Seamlessly bridges the gap between structural vehicle fabrication (hardware point-design trade-offs) and operational mission command (countdown Go/No-Go team protocols).
  • Reactive AI Flight Advisory: Features contextual AI flight directors (Commander Aestro and Chief Engineer Maya) that perform live structural analysis, alerting players to dynamic pressure (Max-Q) hazards, thermal limits, or staging delta-V shortfalls.
  • Integrated 6-Resource Telemetry Matrix: Concurrently balances Fuel Capacity, Electrical Power, Thermal Dissipation, Structural Integrity, Communication Latency, and Scientific Payload Yield.

6. Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Scientific Rigor vs. Gameplay Intuition: Strictly preserving real-world physical laws while maintaining an engaging, accessible learning curve for non-aerospace audiences.
  • Universal Zero-Install Accessibility: Engineered with lightweight WebGL shaders and optimized asset pipelines, allowing the simulation to run fluidly on low-spec laptops, Chromebooks, and tablets without discrete GPUs.
  • Authentic Human-in-the-Loop Collaboration: Ensuring that mission success requires genuine communication and consensus between all four specialized mission control operators.
